issues.description: The Person class in the solution declares the first-name field as 'forename' but all getters/setters and equals/hashCode refer to 'firstName'. The template and tests expect a 'firstName' field. This name mismatch in the solution leads to compilation errors and a broken API surface compared to the template/tests, preventing students from running or comparing against the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution's Person.java, make the field name consistent with the template and tests. Replace 'private String forename;' with 'private String firstName;' (or alternatively update all getters/setters, equals, and hashCode to consistently use 'forename' and adjust template/tests accordingly). Ensure all references (getFirstName, setFirstName, equals, hashCode) compile against the declared field name.

issues.description: The Person entity's first-name attribute is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template and tests use the identifier 'firstName' (with matching getters/setters), while the solution's Person.java declares the field as 'forename'. This creates a confusing mismatch for students mapping the domain concept "first name" to code: tests and other code call getFirstName()/setFirstName(...) but the solution's field name differs, increasing extraneous cognitive load and making comparison between template, tests, and solution unclear.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the first-name attribute across all artifacts. Rename the field in solution/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java from 'forename' to 'firstName' (or alternatively rename template/tests usages to 'forename'), and ensure getters/setters and equals/hashCode reference the same identifier so students can clearly map the domain concept to the code.
